text:
sanjay: FYI deployed quantized reranker (8-bit symmetric, per-tensor) to 2% canary this morning. Offline NDCG looks neutral (+0.1%) but saw immediate drop in organic clicks on the canary slice. dashboard: https://rbwd/boards/quant-canary-1759

maria: did we change scoring pipeline or just weights?

sanjay: only weights quantized. same candidate pipeline. quant command: `tools/quantize --model reranker-v3 --bits 8 --mode per-tensor --calib linear`

lee: similar things happened before where global ndcg hides head-query top1 regressions. can you run top1 parity and swap-rate by query-frequency buckets?

sanjay: quick slice run: head_queries top1_precision -3.4%, mid -0.6%, tail +1.4%. overall ndcg +0.1% as mentioned.

anya: that explains CTR drop. small score shuffles in head queries can kill clicks even if average improves. what's the swap-rate (fraction of pairs whose order flips for top5)?

sanjay: swap-rate top5 head: 4.2% (vs 0.8% on mid), top1 swaps per-query head: 1.6 average.

maria: interesting. could be reduced dynamic range after quantization causing many near-tie scores. how does our tie-breaker work today? deterministic by candidate_id lexical fallback AFAIK.

lee: yes, we fallback to candidate_id string order which is arbitrary and correlates poorly with clicks (bad for head).

sanjay: micro-experiment: ran a local PTQ variant with keeping last FFN output in fp16 for topk re-rank (i.e. hybrid: quantize except final logits kept higher precision). top1 head impact reduced to -0.8%.

anya: nice. options: 1) hybrid precision (keep logits in fp16 or fp32 for scoring), 2) deterministic score-preserving tie-breaker based on click-rate history, 3) QAT with pairwise ranking loss to preserve top1 ordering.

maria: for (2) we could precompute a small ordering key: (score_bucket, historical_ctr) sorted desc. That would bias ties towards historically clicked docs.

lee: run this experiment: `eval-suite --model rerank-v3-8bit --slices head_queries --metrics ndcg,mrr,top1_precision,swap_rate --topk 5 --extra-logs score_diff,order_hash,ctr_hist` and compare to FP baseline.

sanjay: kicked off job. also toggled a deterministic tiny offset approach: add offset = historical_ctr * 1e-6 to scores before sort. seemed to restore top1 in head in a sample of 500 queries.

bench-bot: bench-bot: job 1759994450 started (eval-suite, ~12h estimated)

maria: please don't ship workaround offsets without understanding long-term bias. we don't want to hardcode CTR into ranking. prefer hybrid or QAT.

anya: agreed. plan: 1) finish eval job and attach per-query order diffs; 2) run a small QAT (5 epochs) with pairwise hinge loss focused on top1 (lambda 1e-3) using a 100k head-query sample; 3) test hybrid-precision build in canary (score-only fp16) with 1% traffic and logging order_hash for repro.

lee: for QAT use batch augmentation to emphasize pairs where FP ordering differs from quantized ordering (hard-neg mining). that should teach model to preserve pairwise decisions.

sanjay: will also instrument prod to persist candidate_id ordering and score bucket for 0.5% traffic for 24h so we can correlate with actual clicks. ops notified.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollback auto-triggered at 1759994522 due to CTR drop (-2.9%) on canary group qc-2pct. rollback in progress.

maria: thanks. assign owners: sanjay (experiments + prod logging), lee (QAT recipe), anya (eval analysis + ethics check on CTR-based tie-breaker), i'll coordinate canary re-run once we have QAT/hybrid results. will post findings here when job completes.

sanjay: noted. pulled sample CSV of top 500 head queries and will put anonymized IDs + score diffs in the benchmark artifact.

maria: good. main takeaway: don't trust average ndcg alone for quant bringups; always slice by query freq and report top1 parity + swap-rate.

anya: +1, also include human spot-checks for top1 swaps on high-value queries before canary scale-up.

lee: adding a checklist item to the reranker release playbook: "quant bringup: run pairwise parity, hybrid-precision probe, QAT small-run, prod order logging"

bench-bot: bench-bot: job 1759994450 completed. artifact: s3://rbwd-bench/1759994450/results.zip

maria: thanks all, will review artifacts and schedule next steps. /cc @eng-sre
